EDC mock B

Instructions

  • Time allowed: 2 hours, strictly timed. Sit it in one go, the day before the exam.
  • Open book (hard copy notes, your reference sheet, textbooks). Calculator allowed. No internet.
  • 11 questions, 80 marks. Answer all of them. The marks for each part are in square brackets.
  • Show your working. Write the formula first, then the numbers, then the answer with units. Most marks are for method.
  • The paper is about 45 % diodes and BJTs (Q1 part, Q2–Q6) and about 55 % FETs, multistage, op-amp and power (Q1 part, Q7–Q11).
  • Budget about 1.5 minutes per mark. If a part has taken twice its budget, write down what you would do next and move on.
  • Unless a question says otherwise: Si diodes and BJTs have V, V, , capacitors are short circuits at signal frequency, and is ignored for BJTs.
  • Every circuit is described in words. Draw it yourself before you start each question. The drawing is part of the method.

Question 1 [8 marks]

Circle the correct answer in each part (I to VIII). [1 mark each]

I. Silicon at 300 K ( cm) is doped with donors at cm. The hole concentration is about:

  1. cm b) cm c) cm d) zero

II. A bridge rectifier and a centre-tapped full-wave rectifier are each designed to give the same peak output . Compared with the centre-tapped circuit, each diode in the bridge must withstand a peak inverse voltage of about:

  1. twice as much b) the same c) half as much d) zero, because the bridge diodes never reverse-bias

III. A BJT is in saturation. Which statement is true?

  1. Only the base–emitter junction is forward biased, and
  2. Both junctions are forward biased, and
  3. Both junctions are reverse biased, and
  4. Only the collector–base junction is forward biased, and

IV. An n-channel depletion-type MOSFET with mA and V is biased at V, with large. Then:

  1. the device is cut off
  2. because the gate is positive
  3. the device is in enhancement mode and
  4. the gate draws a large current because the gate junction is forward biased

V. A CMOS inverter running from 5 V has V, V, V and V. Its noise margins are:

  1. V, V b) V c) V d) V, V

VI. A differential amplifier has differential gain and common-mode gain . Its CMRR is:

  1. 40 dB b) 60 dB c) 80 dB d) 10 000 dB

VII. The main cause of crossover distortion in a class B push-pull output stage is that:

  1. the output transformer saturates at high current
  2. neither transistor conducts until its base–emitter voltage reaches about 0.7 V, so there is a dead band near zero
  3. both transistors conduct for the full cycle
  4. the supply voltage is too high

VIII. A basic two-transistor BJT current mirror uses matched transistors with . The ratio is about:

  1. 0.50 b) 0.962 c) 0.980 d) 1.04

Question 2 [7 marks]

(a) A silicon bar is 2 mm long with a square cross-section of 0.1 mm × 0.1 mm. It is doped with boron at cm. Use cm²/Vs, cm²/Vs and, at 300 K, cm.

  1. Find the hole and electron concentrations at 300 K. [1]
  2. Find the conductivity and the resistance of the bar between its two end faces at 300 K. [2]
  3. Use the formula in the table to find at 200 °C. Is the bar still extrinsic (that is, is still a good assumption)? Justify with a number. [1]

(b) A silicon diode with is connected in series with a resistor kΩ across a DC supply V (anode towards the supply, cathode to ground). A small sinusoidal signal of 20 mV peak is connected in series with the 5 V supply. Use V for the DC analysis at 27 °C.

  1. At 27 °C, find the DC diode current, the small-signal resistance , and the peak ac voltage across the diode. [2]
  2. The temperature rises to 77 °C. Using the course temperature rule for , find the new DC current, the new and the new peak ac voltage across the diode. Explain in one sentence why went up even though went up. [1]

Question 3 [5 marks]

Use the constant-voltage diode model with V.

(a) Two-level parallel clipper. The input V is applied to one end of a 1 kΩ series resistor. The other end of the resistor is the output node , which has no load. Two branches go from the output node to ground:

  • Branch 1: diode D1 with its anode at the output node and its cathode at the positive terminal of a 4 V battery. The battery’s negative terminal is grounded.
  • Branch 2: diode D2 with its cathode at the output node and its anode at the negative terminal of a 6 V battery. The battery’s positive terminal is grounded.

Find the two clipping levels and the phase angles ( in degrees) at which each clipping starts and stops. Describe the output waveform over one cycle in words, as you would label a sketch. [3]

(b) Biased clamper. A ±8 V, 1 kHz square wave is applied to a 1 µF capacitor in series. The other plate of the capacitor is the output node. From the output node to ground there is a 100 kΩ resistor, and also a diode with its anode at the output node and its cathode at the positive terminal of a 2 V battery, whose negative terminal is grounded. Find the two output levels and the peak-to-peak output. Describe the output waveform in words. State why the 100 kΩ resistor does not upset the result. [2]

  4. Find the peak diode current (use ). [1]
  5. Find the peak inverse voltage each diode must withstand. [1]

Question 3 (5 marks)

Solution

(a) Find each diode’s turn-on condition from the node voltage.

  • D2 (cathode at , anode at −6 V) conducts when −6.7 V. Then is held at −6.7 V. [1]
  • In between, both diodes are off, no current flows in the 1 kΩ resistor, and .

Transition angles from :

  • Positive clipping: . Clipped from 23.1° to 156.9°.
  • Negative clipping: . Clipped from 213.9° to 326.1°.

Sketch description: the output follows the sine from 0 V up to +4.7 V at 23.1°. It stays flat at +4.7 V until 156.9°, then follows the sine down through 0 V at 180° to −6.7 V at 213.9°. It stays flat at −6.7 V until 326.1°, then follows the sine back up to 0 V at 360°. The output is an asymmetric flat-topped sine. Its top is at +4.7 V, its bottom is at −6.7 V, and it is 11.4 V peak-to-peak. [1]

(b) Start in the half-cycle where the diode conducts. In the +8 V half, the output tries to rise, so the diode turns on and holds +2.7 V. The capacitor charges to V (input side positive).

In the −8 V half, the diode turns off, and the capacitor’s 5.3 V adds to the input: −13.3 V. The diode is reverse biased (−13.3 V < 2.7 V), which confirms it is off. [1]

Sketch description: a square wave of the same shape and frequency (1 kHz). It sits at +2.7 V for the first half-period and at −13.3 V for the second. It is 16 V peak-to-peak, the same as the input, and its average is −5.3 V. The whole input waveform has been shifted down by 5.3 V.

ms, which is 200 times the 0.5 ms half-period. The capacitor barely discharges, so the output is flat (tilt under 0.5 %). [1]

Common mistakes: placing the clip at the battery voltage without the 0.7 V; getting the sign of the D2 level wrong (read which battery terminal the diode touches); for the clamper, starting the analysis in the half-cycle where the diode is off; giving an output peak-to-peak value different from the input’s.

Reread: E3 (clippers and clampers, playbooks E and F).

Night-before checklist

Pack the bag

Ten reflexes to have ready (read once, then sleep)

  1. Units first. Convert °C to K. Put semiconductor lengths in cm. Use in eV/K inside .
  2. Diodes: write the state you assume, find where it changes ( at the transition), then sketch under and label the levels and angles in words.
  3. Full-wave means , and a bridge loses two diode drops while its PIV is only one secondary peak.
  4. BJT DC: use Thevenin and the exact formula. For a pnp, flip every arrow. Always check (or ) against 0.2 V. If it fails, redo the analysis with the saturation model; do not keep .
  5. Small-signal: do DC first, then or , then , , , then the load, then the source divider. Watch the sign: CE, CS and drain feedback invert; CB and followers do not.
  6. FET quadratics: keep the root with between (or ) and the right side of the curve. A D-MOSFET may have a positive and , and that is fine.
  7. . Use whenever it is given.
  8. Cascades: load each stage with the next stage’s , then multiply. Two inverting stages give a positive gain.
  9. Power: . Class A transformer-coupled is 50 %; class B is 78.5 %. Class B dissipation peaks at .
  10. Digital and op-amp: , , and CMRR(dB) .

In the exam room

Sleep by a sensible hour. A rested brain is worth more than one more pack tonight.
